base_meanings: Befehlen; die Gewalt zu schaffen haben / mandar, ejercer autoridad
historical.source_relation: Merrill explicitly summarizes selíameke ‘juez del pueblo, gobernante’ as derived from selí ‘gobernar’, based on Steffel entries E-0582/E-0583 and parallel manuscript witnesses.
historical.stress: Selí is final-stressed; the derived form preserves stress on the lexical material as Selíameke in the critical edition.

modern_independent_choguita.source: Caballero 2022, A grammar of Choguita Rarámuri
modern_independent_choguita.context: singular member of a nominal singular/pluractional paradigm; plural/pluractional i-ˈsêrikame
modern_independent_choguita.general_morphology: Caballero independently lists -ame as the participial suffix in Choguita Rarámuri.
modern_independent_choguita.lexeme_specific_segmentation: not explicitly provided in the audited table; the surface ending -ame is therefore noted without mechanically imposing segmentation on siˈríame.

modern_src02.warning: The exact-string modern base pair is false; Siríami is retained because of historical and independent Choguita evidence, not because of those homonyms.
modern_src02.provenance: SRC-02 file identity unresolved and likely within a Hilton/pre-2016 lexicographic lineage.

pretonic_e_i.historical_general_variation: Merrill documents e~i variation elsewhere in Steffel, including síneví~síniví and taitéke~taitéki.
pretonic_e_i.modern_independent_process: Caballero documents optional /e/ raising to [i] in pretonic/posttonic position, including neˈhê~niˈhê and beˈnè~biˈnè.
pretonic_e_i.assessment: independently plausible; no directional diachronic sound law is claimed

liquid_l_r.historical_source_statement: Steffel treats L and R among ‘letras equívocas’ that can interchange without changing the word/meaning in relevant cases, as reported and analyzed by Merrill.
liquid_l_r.merrill_general_analysis: Merrill documents l~r alternation in Steffel while also preserving contexts where the liquids contrast.
liquid_l_r.independent_same_morphological_domain_co: cavólameke ~ cavórameke ‘esférico/redondo’ is explicitly treated by Merrill as medial <l>~<r> alternation inside an -ameke form.
liquid_l_r.assessment: strong historical plausibility for Selí~Siri at the liquid position; not a license to neutralize l/r globally

participial_surface.historical: Steffel explicitly treats ameke as participial and reports frequent omission of final ke; Merrill analyzes relevant historical chains with participial -(a)me plus optional reduplicative -kV/-ke.
participial_surface.modern_independent: Caballero independently documents productive participial -ame; siˈríame has a surface final -ame.
participial_surface.assessment: very strong constructional compatibility, but the audited Caballero paradigm does not itself segment siˈríame morpheme-by-morpheme

integrated_formal_assessment.pretonic_vowel_difference: e~i independently supported historically and synchronically
integrated_formal_assessment.liquid_difference: l~r independently attested within Steffel, including another -ameke lexical item
integrated_formal_assessment.participial_domain_difference: historical -ameke versus independent Choguita surface -ame; source-level analyses make this difference structurally plausible

competing_etymological_tradition.source: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura, ‘Sistema normativo de los rarámuri de Chihuahua’
competing_etymological_tradition.claim: A cultural-historical synthesis states that pre-Jesuit spear-bearing authorities were called selígame ‘portador de lanza’, derived there from selaka ‘lanza’, and that the governor later came to be called siríame.
competing_etymological_tradition.conflict_or_tension: This differs from the Steffel/Merrill analysis selí ‘gobernar’ -> selíameke ‘gobernante/juez del pueblo’.
competing_etymological_tradition.rule: Do not merge selígame/selaka and selí/selíameke analyses until the original sources behind the SIC synthesis are traced and the forms are compared philologically.

why_grade_A: Steffel preserves an explicit base/derived pair Selí ‘gobernar’ -> Selíameke ‘gobernante/juez del pueblo’.
Caballero independently documents Choguita siˈríame ‘governor(s)’ and productive participial -ame in the same modern grammar.
The target pretonic e~i difference has independent historical and modern Rarámuri controls.
The l~r difference has an explicit historical alternation and a same-domain control cavólameke~cavórameke.
The historical -ameke versus modern surface -ame relation is independently grounded by Steffel's ke-omission statement and Merrill/Caballero analyses.
The candidate therefore survives source-independence and formal-correspondence controls without relying on SRC-02.
remaining_limits: Grade A is an evidential-architecture judgment, not a declaration of cognacy.
Caballero's table does not explicitly segment siˈríame as siri + -ame; productive -ame makes the surface relation highly relevant but does not replace lexeme-specific analysis.
The competing selígame<selaka spear-bearer etymology must be audited before a publication-level derivational history is selected.
No general sound laws e>i or l>r are declared from this item.
SRC-02 Siríami is supplementary because its documentary independence from Hilton is unresolved.
next_tests: Trace the references behind the SIC selígame/selaka explanation and locate the earliest explicit source for that etymology.
Search independent modern varieties and community texts for siríame/serígame and, if possible, verbal siri/seri forms.
Determine whether the Choguita plural/pluractional form i-ˈsêrikame provides internal stem evidence relevant to siriame beyond the general participial analysis.
Keep the two historical derivational hypotheses separate until source-level reconciliation is possible.
